title: Keyboard Manager Issue
author: GrayPlasma
summary: The remap targets logical VK_END, so it also affects numpad 1 when Num Lock is off; physical-key-specific remapping is tracked by #16432.

confidence.rationale: The public discussion and linked ownership evidence support this classification.

judgment.rationale: Keyboard Manager remaps logical virtual keys, so physical End and numpad 1 with Num Lock off can both emit VK_END. The request to distinguish physical keys sharing one logical function is already tracked in #16432.
evidence: Disabling End also disables numpad 1 when it emits the End virtual key.
The discussion links #16432, which requests remapping only one physical key rather than every key with the same function.
The reporter has not supplied a newer result that distinguishes this from the known virtual-key behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: The requested physical-key distinction is tracked in #16432 and should not receive a parallel fix plan here.

issue_context.summary: The remap targets logical VK_END, so it also affects numpad 1 when Num Lock is off; physical-key-specific remapping is tracked by #16432.
known_information: The affected keys are physical End and numpad 1 in its End state.
Issue #16432 remains open for distinguishing physical keys with the same logical function.
inferences: The saved remap is behaving according to Keyboard Manager's virtual-key identity model.
Changing this requires scan-code/physical-key support rather than a one-off End-key exception.
issue_context.analysis: This is a known product-model limitation with a canonical enhancement. A separate bug design would duplicate #16432.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the live body, both comments, current labels, and the referenced canonical issue.

actions.label: Close as physical-key remapping duplicate
actions.note: Draft only; no comment, close, label, or other write was made to microsoft/PowerToys.

comment.body: Thanks for clarifying the End/numpad behavior. Keyboard Manager currently remaps the logical `VK_END`, and numpad 1 emits that same logical key when Num Lock is off. Distinguishing the physical End key from other keys with the same function is tracked in #16432, so this issue can be closed as a duplicate and continued there.
